facts.text: Funkstown began in 1754 when Henry Funk purchased 88 acres from Frederick Calvert, the 6th Baron Baltimore, and the settlement was originally named Jerusalem.
During the Civil War, a strong Confederate presence at Funkstown threatened any Union advance against General Lee.
On July 10, 1863, John Buford's Federal cavalry cautiously approached Funkstown via the National Road, encountering Stuart's crescent-shaped battle line.
The day-long battle east of Funkstown resulted in 479 casualties, a toll that echoed the fierce fighting of Gettysburg.
Funkstown Historic District was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2000, preserving its 18th‑century architecture.
Antietam Creek flows south through Funkstown, joining the Potomac River just south of Hagerstown.
